statement: Let n = len(team). A catch pair is a pair (i, j) of indices with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, team[i] = 1, team[j] = 0, and |i - j| <= dist (absolute value of the integer difference i - j). A catching assignment is a set M of catch pairs such that no two pairs of M have the same first component and no two pairs of M have the same second component (equivalently: each person who is "it" catches at most one person, and each person who is not "it" is caught at most once). The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum possible size of a catching assignment: there exists a catching assignment M with |M| = r, and every catching assignment M' satisfies |M'| <= r.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team) (so dist >= 0).

statement: Let ones = the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(team) and team[i] = 1, and zeros = the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(team) and team[j] = 0. The function returns a result r with 0 <= r <= min(ones, zeros).
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: The function returns the result r = 0.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, 1 <= dist <= len(team), and team[i] = 0 for every i with 0 <= i < len(team) (there is no person who is "it").

statement: Let n = len(team). The returned value r satisfies: r = 0 if and only if there is no pair of indices (i, j) with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, team[i] = 1, team[j] = 0 and |i - j| <= dist. Equivalently, r >= 1 if and only if some person who is "it" is within distance dist of some person who is not "it".
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: Let r be the returned value. Then there exist r distinct indices j_1, ..., j_r with 0 <= j_k < len(team) and team[j_k] = 0, and r distinct indices i_1, ..., i_r with 0 <= i_k < len(team) and team[i_k] = 1, such that |i_k - j_k| <= dist for every k with 1 <= k <= r. (In other words, r distinct people who are not "it" can simultaneously be caught, each by a distinct person who is "it" within distance dist.)
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: Let n = len(team) and let reachable = the number of indices j with 0 <= j < n, team[j] = 0, for which there exists an index i with 0 <= i < n, team[i] = 1 and |i - j| <= dist. The returned value r satisfies r <= reachable.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: Let ones = the number of indices i with team[i] = 1 and zeros = the number of indices j with team[j] = 0. The function returns the result r = min(ones, zeros).
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team), and additionally dist >= len(team) - 1.

statement: Let n = len(team) and let rev be the array of length n defined by rev[i] = team[n - 1 - i] for 0 <= i < n (the order of all people is reversed). Then the maximum number of people who can be caught from rev with the same distance dist is equal to the returned value r for team.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: Let r be the returned value for distance dist. For every integer dist' with dist <= dist' <= len(team), the maximum number of people who can be caught from the same array team with distance dist' is at least r.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: Let i be that unique index with team[i] = 1. The function returns r = 1 if there exists an index j with 0 <= j < len(team), team[j] = 0 and |i - j| <= dist; otherwise it returns r = 0.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, 1 <= dist <= len(team), and there is exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(team) and team[i] = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r (i.e. it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic) for every input satisfying the preconditions; moreover 0 <= r <= len(team) <= 100000, so the returned value fits in a 64-bit integer.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, len(team) <= 100000, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).

statement: Let n = len(team) and let p be an index with 0 <= p < n - 1 such that no catch crosses the cut between p and p + 1, i.e. for all indices i, j with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, team[i] = 1, team[j] = 0, it is not the case that (i <= p and j > p and j - i <= dist) and it is not the case that (i > p and j <= p and i - j <= dist). Let r_left be the maximum number of pairwise-disjoint catch pairs (i, j) with i <= p and j <= p (within the left part), and r_right the maximum number of pairwise-disjoint catch pairs with i > p and j > p (within the right part), where a catch pair (i, j) means team[i] = 1, team[j] = 0 and |i - j| <= dist. Then the returned value satisfies r = r_left + r_right.
preconditions: len(team) >= 1, every element of team is 0 or 1, and 1 <= dist <= len(team).
